A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CODiff and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. All ten pages of each were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 report original restoration results, computational measurements, component ablations and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains the original quantitative experiments and ablations and presents revised qualitative restoration examples in Figure 5.

M1.justification: Section 3, Figure 3 and Equations 1–10 retain the same two-stage CODiff procedure: dual learning for CaVE, LoRA adaptation, perceptual and GAN objectives, and one-step restoration.

E1.justification: Both train on DF2K and LSDIR and evaluate JPEG restoration on LIVE-1, Urban100 and DIV2K-Val. The compression levels illustrated by the revised Figure 5 already occur in v1's evaluations or analyses; the changed examples do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FBCNN, JDEC, PromptCIR, DiffBIR*, SUPIR and OSEDiff*. Figure 5 retains its comparator set, and Table 3 retains the same prompt alternatives. Newly cited OSCAR is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Figure 5 changes the qualitative examples and crops from QF=5 throughout to QF=1, 5 and 10. The main benchmark protocol, metrics, training budgets and computational-comparison settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 5 revises the qualitative cases examining artifact suppression and detail preservation, replacing two QF=5 cases with QF=1 and QF=10 examples. Component and loss ablations in Tables 3–5, embedding analyses in Figures 2 and 4, and unseen-QF prediction analysis in Figure 7 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both retain point estimates and the same QF-prediction MSE plots; these plots measure prediction error rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: All numerical values in Tables 1–5 are unchanged. Figure 5 replaces the LIVE-1 ocean and Urban100 building examples at QF=5 with Urban100 examples labeled img_091 at QF=1 and img_080 at QF=10, retaining the DIV2K-Val fox at QF=5. These are replacement qualitative results under different samples, crops or settings.

T1.justification: The diffusion formulation, compression-embedding definition and loss equations remain unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both retain the claims of a compression-prior-guided one-step JPEG restoration model, dual learning for CaVE, and strong restoration quality with reduced computation. The abstract edits do not substantively alter the contributions or novelty claims.

C2.justification: Explanations linking restoration quality and generalization to compression priors and dual learning remain unchanged, as does the efficiency explanation concerning auxiliary modules. Revised descriptions of image details introduce no new mechanism, applicability boundary or limitation.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promise to release code and models with a statement that code is available at the same repository. Section 4.4 removes the '(e.g., QF=1)' cue from the Table 3 description without supplying a replacement setting; this reduces documented specificity without establishing an experimental change. Other implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds OSCAR: One-Step Diffusion Codec Across Multiple Bit-Rates as reference 11. Existing cited works and the paper's compression-prior positioning remain intact; most citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: There are brief edits to the abstract, related-work wording and qualitative-results paragraph, updated affiliations and contact formatting, and added acknowledgments. The main section organization and methodological exposition remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 5 replaces two comparison rows, relocates the retained fox example and revises its caption to emphasize compression levels. Figures 2 and 4 receive small sizing or alignment adjustments. Table structures and the overall two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Figure 5 now illustrates restoration across QF=1, 5 and 10, providing more informative visual support across compression severities, and the abstract reports available code. These are modest gains, tempered by removing Table 3's QF=1 cue and thus reducing experimental specificity. The method, numerical validation and central conclusions remain unchanged.
